properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:55PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
rise through Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a
gradual rise through the week, and may approach its record flood.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Monday was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 6.1 feet late this week. Additional rises
are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:52PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Sanford
to continue rising through Moderate Flood Stage. The river is
forecast to climb into Major Flood stage around mid-week, remaining
steady around 8.2 feet through late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 7.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Monday was 7.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise into Major Flood Stage,
reaching 8.2 feet mid week.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:49PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to hold near a crest through tomorrow before beginning a
very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 13.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 13.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to gradually fall through this
week, remaining within Major Flood Stage.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:46PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends will remain
generally steady near 18.5 ft or 18.6 ft through late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 18.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM EST Monday was 18.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady between 18.5
and 18.6 feet through late week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:43PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above Major
Flood Stage, slowly reaching 4.4 feet late this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

warned area.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:59AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 856 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 2.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:36 AM
Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.
* West Sacramento: 2.2 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 2:49
PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM
Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.4 ft at 2:00 PM Mon 11/23,
+7.5 ft at 2:45 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.6 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
